name: Totem
description: Modular hardware for running napplets on user-controlled devices connected over a FIPS mesh. Two Totem prototypes found each other during SEC-08; the platform remains experimental.

name: Napplets
description: NIP-5D's small, sandboxed Nostr apps advanced across SEC-08. Host shells handle signing, relay access and storage so the same focused app can run in different environments.

name: FIPS Native Datagrams
description: Experimental public-key-addressed application traffic that bypasses the usual IP stack. This early native API was demonstrated during SEC-08; it was not a FIPS v2 release.

name: Wok over FIPS
description: A Nostr relay transport experiment using native FIPS datagrams. JeffG measured faster relay messages in the cohort demo, with performance varying by message size.

name: White Noise over FIPS
description: SEC-08 demo of encrypted Marmot group chat carried through a relay using native FIPS transport; an integration experiment rather than a released default transport.

name: FipWave
description: Sends FIPS packets over sound. In the demo, two laptops exchanged data across a room using their speakers and microphones.

name: fips-exit-gate
description: An experimental FIPS exit gateway for reaching services on the legacy internet from the mesh.

name: fips-shield
description: Application-level protection work for services exposed through FIPS, developed alongside André's mesh gateway experiments.

name: fips2go
description: Android VPN host for carrying phone traffic through FIPS and discovering nearby peers without manual setup.

name: FIPS Mac
description: Mac menu-bar tooling to install and run a FIPS node and inspect the mesh. Peer allowlist and blocklist work was proposed in an open contribution.

name: FIPS Relay Tray
description: FIPS integration for nostr-relay-tray, bringing a desktop Nostr relay onto the mesh.

name: FIPS on FreeBSD
description: Exploratory FreeBSD packaging and service support for FIPS, including TUN integration work.

name: fipsd
description: A workbench for FIPS protocol experiments and visualizations. Some features model possible behavior rather than running a complete network.

name: LUKS over FIPS
description: A demo of remotely unlocking an encrypted NixOS drive through the FIPS mesh.

name: FIPS Pong
description: A browser bridge carried a three-machine Pong demo over FIPS native transport: a playful proof of the transport.

name: CruxCoach
description: Climbing companions sync board playlists across a local BLE and FIPS mesh, even without internet. The team also explored bringing MoonBoard logs across via Android accessibility tools.

name: RocketShell
description: A browser host for NostrRocket napplets. It keeps signing, relay access and storage in the shell while small apps handle one task each.

name: Uzel
description: A native Debian host for running napplets outside a browser, explored during SEC-08's runtime work.

name: nampplets
description: An in-progress Rust runtime with a macOS reference host for native napplets.

name: Napplet Portal
description: A server-backed napplet host that lets people open Nostr apps from a phone browser.

name: Envelope
description: An nsite-hosted napplet runtime that can carry app state inside a link, so a small app and its state can travel together.

name: Nostrocket Napplets
description: Composable problem-tracker napplets for opening, viewing and editing work inside NostrRocket. One action can open the next focused tool.

name: Rage of Empires
description: A reconstructed Age of Empires game packed into one HTML file, demonstrated in multiplayer as both a napplet and an nsite.

name: Myco
description: Nearby phones share apps and files across Bluetooth or FIPS; file sharing also gained a hotspot and web route for peers without Myco.

name: Nappagochi
description: A Nostr pet whose changing life reflects your activity on the network.

name: Anon&Mato
description: A playable world generated from a player's npub and choices, presented as a cohort game demo.

name: XR Napplets
description: A proof of concept for rendering napplets on augmented-reality glasses, shown during the final demo week.

name: stlstr
description: Shares 3D printable models through small napplets for discovery, previews and detail views.

name: SEC-08 Napplet Workshop
description: Small napplets for saving notes and checking profile and media health, built as concrete examples during Gigi's SEC-08 workshop.

name: CAHMLS
description: An ad-hoc Cordn coordinator that runs in a browser tab, explored as part of SEC-08's messaging experiments.

name: Paja
description: A long-form writing tool for drafting and scheduling Nostr posts, demonstrated in the cohort notes.

name: nixstr-cache
description: Serves Nix packages from Blossom blobs discovered through Nostr and Hashtree, while keeping Nix's own cache-signature checks.

name: Narwal
description: A Nix cache proxy that resolves package data via Nostr and Hashtree and fetches blobs from Blossom for ordinary Nix clients.

name: Hashtree Explainer
description: An interactive explanation of how directories can be addressed by hash and distributed as blobs.

name: Nostrpkgs
description: Packages Nostr software for reproducible installation, part of Julien's SEC-08 distribution work.

name: ngit-deploy
description: Explores deployment from Nostr-native Git repositories as part of the cohort's software distribution experiments.

name: deno2nix
description: Packages Deno applications with Nix so they can join reproducible build and distribution workflows.

name: nix-golsim
description: A reproducible Conway's Game of Life visualization built with Nix during the cohort's packaging experiments.

name: Mapplets
description: Map tiles fetched as Hashtree and Blossom data, with Nostr events for place information, Madeira bus routes and selected overlays.

name: Mapeira
description: Transforms outside map and transport information into queryable Nostr events used by Mapplets.

name: Just Works
description: Merchant nsites assembled from existing business information, with Nostr identity, a map, QR codes and Lightning point-of-sale flows.

name: keys.justworks
description: Key storage and signing access for merchants using Just Works, keeping that responsibility underneath the storefront.

name: Granola
description: Testnet proof of concept for coordinating Cashu atomic swaps over Nostr. The Cashu mints still settle the swap.

name: Upay
description: An escrow and arbiter experiment for peer-to-peer Cashu trades, demonstrated during SEC-08.

name: 600 Billion Timelock TCG
description: A trading card game on Nappelin where cards are Cashu tokens; NUT-22 blinded tokens are explored to keep a player's hand private.

name: NutFT
description: An exploratory proposal for collectible assets represented by Cashu tokens; its draft NUT number is not an official assignment.

name: Meza
description: A cohort demo for zapping highlighted passages and splitting payments among the author, highlighter and reading app.

name: net4sats
description: A Wi-Fi access business experiment that sells connectivity for bitcoin, with a branded captive portal built on TollGate.

name: Nostrology
description: Nostr ecosystem metrics and marketplace maps exposed to people and agents, including Cashu-paid Nutzap data queries.

name: Nectar
description: Explores structured, attestable datasets on Nostr for queries and agent use.

name: si-eval
description: Auditable model-evaluation experiments on consequential tasks such as key handling and privacy.

name: Mist
description: A Nostr conversation client that explores threads as clusters instead of a single linear timeline.

name: Mappy
description: Explores agents helping with real-world map tasks. Its map events can include encrypted descriptions while coordinates remain public tags.

name: Kipina
description: An agent inside a napplet, connecting to a local harness through ContextVM tooling.

name: fips.email
description: Turns email sent to an npub address into encrypted NIP-17 direct messages for people or agents. Despite its name, the service does not use FIPS.

name: JamCore
description: A collaborative music experiment that listens and adapts to players, with future agent accompaniment explored in the demo.

name: Demo Day Command Center
description: A captain's tracker and timer for Friday demos, with feedback and exports to keep the lineup moving.

name: Nowhere CLI
description: A command-line tool for creating and managing websites without a hosted dashboard.

name: Cashu Sync
description: An experiment in synchronizing Cashu wallet state for Silent Link across devices.

name: terrDVM
description: A Data Vending Machine experiment for generating terrain models from geographic inputs.

name: bimCVP
description: Coordinates and checks building models as part of the cohort's construction-data experiments.

name: DJ David Clanker
description: A music agent that plays Wavlake tracks, built among the cohort's playful agent experiments.

name: Avatar
description: An experimental pipeline for creating digital characters for app and game work.

name: Scored Relay
description: An experimental relay that ranks Nostr events by proof of work and recency.

name: SNIPER
description: A relay experiment for installable NIP extensions, explored during SEC-08.

name: Rustic Applesauce
description: Rust tools for composing Nostr client operations, developed alongside SEC-08's napplet and runtime work.

name: guerrilla-entropy
description: An experimental hardware entropy contributor. Its own documentation says it is not a certified cryptographic random-number generator.

name: FIPS Globe
description: A visual exploration of FIPS mesh activity shown during SEC-08.

name: Cordn Coordinator
description: An Android coordinator demo for hosting Cordn groups and messaging.

name: Marmot Invite Links
description: An experiment for inviting people into Marmot groups through shareable links outside the core protocol.

name: Marmot Encrypted Images
description: A final-week demo exploring encrypted image and file sharing inside Marmot groups.

name: Nostr Office Concierge
description: A final-week assistant prototype for managing shared spaces at the Nostr Office.

name: Arraia
description: An experiment in sharing vendor locations, goods and payment details over Bitchat.

name: Pyramid Nix Package
description: Nix packaging work for Pyramid, part of Julien's experiments in reproducible software distribution.

name: FIPS NixOS Module
description: A NixOS module and demo configuration for deploying FIPS through reproducible system configuration.

name: Plebeian Market Auctions
description: A cohort experiment adding simple Nostr auctions to Plebeian Market, without an escrow or arbiter flow.
